findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The available certified food manager’s certificates are expired. PIC was informed and stated that process of renewal would be initiated. Ensure that Food certificates should be maintained and monitored.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: The inspectors observed that container of shredded cheese and chicken fingers were found without date marking in the prep cooler in the back. PIC was informed and educated about date marking. Ensure that ready to eat items date marked properly. Dates were added to the items to correct.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Working bottle with chemical observed without labeling. PIC was informed and labeled with appropriate chemical name. Make sure that all working bottom with chemicals shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material/chemical.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Probe thermometers were available however, inspectors found thermometers to be out of calibration and were not reading accurate. Inspectors demonstrated proper way to calibrate of thermometer in and educated. Ensure that thermometers shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use.
findings.citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM) present at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- a CFM arrived towards the end of the inspection. Ensure that there is a CFM present at all times food is being prepared or handled.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The concentration of the prepared sanitizer bucket was initially reading at 0 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- inspector instructed staff member to add a quat tablet to the sanitizer bucket. The sanitizer bucket met the 200 ppm criteria. Use test strips to ensure the correct concentration of sanitizer solution so that that food contact surfaces are properly sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed spatula that was cracked along the perimeter of the food-contact surface. CORRECTED- inspector notified staff member about the condition of the spatula and it was voluntarily discarded. Ensure that food contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.11(A) Food-Contact Surfaces. (A) Multiuse FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be: (1) Smooth; (2) Free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections; (3) Free of sharp internal angles, corners, and crevices. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: No sanitizer bucket was observed in the facility at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was being prepared by a kitchen staff member as the inspectors entered the kitchen. This sanitizer bucket was observed at 0 ppm (see violation #16), and no alternative sanitization method was available. Ensure sanitizer solutions are prepared at the start of a shift where food is being handled.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Two areas at the physical facility were observed to be in need of repair. 
1) The southwest ceiling corner above the soda boxes contains a hole about 3” by 3” in area. Ensure the ceiling tile is moved or the gap is filled to prevent against pest harborage. 
2) The orange splash guard behind the mop sink is not adhered to the wall. Water is present between the splash guard and wall, which could allow for the growth and harborage of mold or bacteria. 
Ensure physical facilities are maintained and repairs are made by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
